holidays.name: National Cherry Pie Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the flaky, tart-and-sweet glory of cherry pie. Bakers and pie lovers alike are encouraged to whip up a lattice-topped masterpiece or simply grab a slice with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
holidays.origin: Cherry Pie Day is an unofficial American food holiday tied to February's association with George Washington's birthday and the legend of the cherry tree. Pie-themed food holidays are popularized through bakery promotions and food calendars.
holidays.funFact: Cherry pie is so tied to American identity that it features in the TV series Twin Peaks, where Special Agent Dale Cooper is famously devoted to it. The George Washington cherry tree story was invented by biographer Parson Weems after Washington's death.

holidays.name: Love Your Pet Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to showering your furry, feathered, scaly, or finned companions with extra treats, cuddles, and attention. Pets everywhere are encouraged to expect the royal treatment.
holidays.origin: Love Your Pet Day was created by the pet lifestyle expert and author Colleen Paige, who is also behind many other pet-focused observances such as National Dog Day and National Cat Day.
holidays.funFact: Colleen Paige founded several pet holidays, including National Puppy Day and National Dog Day, making her one of the most prolific inventors of pet observances in the world.

holidays.name: World Day of Social Justice
holidays.description: An international observance recognizing the need to promote efforts to tackle poverty, exclusion, and unemployment, and to advance fair treatment for all people around the globe.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly designated February 20 as the World Day of Social Justice in 2007, with the first observance held in 2009.
holidays.funFact: The day was proposed as part of the UN's push to turn social development ideals into action, and it is observed in the same month as many other UN-linked awareness days.

holidays.name: Hoodie Hoo Day
holidays.description: At noon local time, participants step outside, raise their arms, and shout 'Hoodie Hoo!' to chase away winter and welcome spring. Neighbors may stare, but that's part of the charm.
holidays.origin: Hoodie Hoo Day is a quirky, unofficial observance reportedly dreamed up in the 1980s, and it has been shared in books of wacky holidays. The idea is that the chant scares winter away.
holidays.funFact: There's no official meaning of the phrase 'Hoodie Hoo,' which is part of the fun, and the whole goal is to get as many people as possible to yell it simultaneously at noon.

holidays.name: National Muffin Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating the humble muffin, in all its blueberry, chocolate chip, and bran-filled variety. It is the perfect excuse to eat cake for breakfast and pretend it is healthy.
holidays.origin: National Muffin Day is an unofficial American food observance promoted through food calendars and bakeries, giving muffin fans a reason to celebrate in the heart of winter.
holidays.funFact: The English muffin and the American muffin are very different foods, and the American-style muffin is essentially a cupcake's breakfast-friendly cousin.
